Usage: recorder [options] [command]

Screen recordings with a movie editor: record the screen, a window or an app
with audio and the cursor, then cut, zoom and export in the recorder window or
from the command line

Options:
  -v, --verbose                               Enable verbose logging
  --readme                                    Print this tool's README and exit
  -h, --help                                  display help for command

Commands:
  start [options]                             Record a movie into the recordings library (screen.mp4 with audio tracks, cursor.jsonl, recording.json), or with --frames the frames of the displays (JPEG or the recorder's files, OCR into ocr.jsonl or beside each frame), as recorder.start() in the REPL does. Runs until the stop command, the menu bar item, the floating controls, Ctrl-C or --max-seconds; pausing leaves the paused time out
  stop [options] [id]                         Stop the live recording (the newest one, or the id given)
  pause [options] [id]                        Pause the live recording (the newest one, or the id given)
  resume [options] [id]                       Resume the live recording (the newest one, or the id given)
  status [options] [id]                       Print the live recording's state (the newest one, or the id given)
  mark [options] <label> [id]                 Mark this moment of the live recording with a label; the editor and movie.markers() show it
  undo [options] <recording>                  Put an edit back as it was before its last change, made with apply, the REPL or the editor window (30 steps, across runs); redo makes it again
  redo [options] <recording>                  Make the last change that undo took back again, while the edit has not changed since that undo
  rename [options] <recording> <title>        Give a recording a new title (the library, the editor window and movies.list() show it)
  import [options] <movie>                    Make a library recording of a movie file (.mp4, .m4v or .mov), titled --title or the file's name, with a marker at each --marker: an APFS clone of it where the disk can make one (no extra disk), else a whole copy, and the file stays as it is; prints its folder, and the editor, movies.open() and every command take its id
  copy [options] <recording>                  Copy a recording's movie (the newest export, else its own movie) to the clipboard as a file; --gif copies a GIF of the edit, exporting one when none is current
  reveal [options] <recording>                Show a recording's folder in Finder; --meeting shows its meeting's record instead
  trash [options] <recording...>              Move library recordings through the removal policy into the GenesisTools trash, all in one call; the answer names the batch, when it drains and the tools rm restore command that puts it back (tools rm trash lists it too; the window's Move to Trash uses Finder's Trash). Run by an agent, or for a recording the policy does not allow, it asks the user: every such recording goes into ONE request they confirm with tools rm approve <id>. A meeting's screen recording is refused, and then nothing is moved
  comment [options] <recording> <at> <text>   Add a review comment at a time of the edit (OUTPUT seconds or m:ss, what plays); the editor shows it as a marker on the timeline. `comment add <recording> <at> <text>` is the same command
  comments [options] <recording>              A recording's review comments in time order, with where each plays in the edit
  resolve [options] <recording> <id>          Mark a review comment done (--reopen opens it again)
  uncomment [options] <recording> <id>        Remove a review comment
  demo [options] <script>                     Record a finished demo from a JSON script of steps: each step is marked, its caption shows while it plays, the waiting between steps is cut, and the movie is exported (the REPL's movies.demo() runs code steps)
  markers [options] <recording>               The moments marked while a recording ran, with where each plays in its edit (null when cut)
  click-groups [options] <recording>          The recorded clicks in groups (as autoZoom groups them), each with its count, source seconds and where it plays
  replace-words [options] <recording>         Replace a word or phrase in every transcript line (captions and subtitles show the fixed words); one undo
  check [options] <recording>                 What to fix before an export (items and markers whose time is cut, texts a cut shortens, missing music, captions or subtitles without a transcript) and what to look at; changes nothing
  items-at [options] <recording> <at>         What plays at an OUTPUT time of the edit, in words: the source time, the picture and canvas zooms, hidden parts, texts, shapes, lenses, the caption line and what is said
  fix [options] <recording>                   Runs every fix `check` offers (removes what never shows, moves a cut marker to the nearest kept moment, lengthens what is too short to read, moves a text off another) in one save and one undo step
  sheet [options] <recording>                 Several frames on one PNG grid, each labelled with its time: the edit as it exports (OUTPUT seconds) or, with --source, the recording as it was recorded (SOURCE seconds, the seconds ops take)
  still [options] <recording> [at]            One frame on a PNG: the edit as it exports at an OUTPUT time, or with --source the recording as recorded at a SOURCE time
  search [options] <text>                     Find a moment across the library: titles, marker labels and cached transcript lines (case and accents ignored)
  list [options]                              The recordings library, newest first (or the running recordings with --live)
  show|info [options] <recording>             One recording's facts as JSON, as a row of list --json: its id, title, folder, start, length, how it ended, frames, movie and whether it was edited
  library [options]                           Open the recordings library window: double-click a recording to edit it
  opened [options]                            The recordings open in the editor and the one in front; `open` names it in every other command
  edit [options] [recording]                  Open a recording or a movie in the recorder's editor window (no recording: pick one)
  window [options]                            The recorder's editor windows: `edit` opens one, `opened` lists them, `window close` closes one
  project [options] <recording>               Print a recording's edit: its clips, zooms, audio and export settings (times in source seconds)
  apply [options] <recording> <ops>           Change a recording's edit with JSON ops, in order, saved once (the open editor window reloads it), e.g. {"op":"cut","from":4,"to":"0:09"}. Ops: split, cut, keep, speed, zoom, unzoom, redact, spotlight, unredact, text, untext, marker, unmarker, retime, shape, unshape, fixLine, unfixLine, autoZoom, annotateClicks, volume, mute, audio, music, exportSettings, reset, clicks, keys, captions, motion, cursor, frame, camera, cameraHide, cameraShow, removeIdle, cutWords, cutFillers, denoise, normalize, lanes, addLane, removeLane, moveLane, moveToLane, setZoom, setRedaction, setText, setShape, trim, deleteClip, clipSpeed, duplicate, removeClickCircles, renameLane, voiceover, unvoiceover, ducking, captionsStyle, progress, introCard, endCard, range, transition, lens, setLens, unlens, tilt, hidePrivate, hideText, cursorSmooth, speedUpWaits, autoSpeed, redactionJoins, unhide; a wrong or missing field names the right ones, and the REPL's help("movies") documents each. Times are source seconds or "mm:ss"
  export [options] <recording>                Render a recording's edit (or a whole movie) to an MP4 with the editor's own renderer, without a window
  finish [options] <recording> <movie>        After an export: write the subtitle file and put the markers into an MP4 as chapters, by the edit's settings
  cut-words [options] <recording>             Cut words out of the transcript line spoken at a source time (every place that line says them, or --occurrence); one undo
  words [options] <recording>                 The words of each transcript line as cut-words splits and times them (the editor's word pick reads this)
  transcribe [options] <recording>            Transcribe what the export plays (every unmuted audio track, on the movie's clock) into the transcript the captions read; a paid run, cached beside the movie
  cut-fillers [options] <recording>           Cut every filler word of the transcript in one step (cs, sk, en lists, or --words); one undo
  subtitles [options] <recording>             Write a recording's transcript as a subtitle file for its export (cut lines left out, fixes kept): the export's clock, so with an intro card every cue starts the card's length later
  proxy [options] <recording>                 Make proxy.mp4 for a frames-only recording (frames at their times, audio pieces mixed in), so the editor opens it
  find-screen [options] <recording> <text>    Where a text was on the screen, at source seconds: a frames recording or a meeting from its OCR, a movie from its screen text (the first search reads it once, which can take minutes)
  duplicate [options] <recording>             Copy a recording with its edit (APFS clones, no extra disk) to a new library recording titled "<title> (copy)", or to --to; prints the copy's edit path
  private-data [options] <recording>          List the private data on a recording's screen (emails, tokens and keys, phone numbers, IBANs, card numbers), read with Vision OCR on this Mac; hide them with the hidePrivate op
  waits [options] <recording>                 List the typing and waiting stretches of a recording (only a small part of the picture changes, or nothing) with a proposed 4x to 8x speed-up; apply them with the speedUpWaits op
  events [options] <recording>                List what happens on a recording's screen at source seconds: scene changes, scrolls, still stretches, clicks, and taps from --taps; place effects on them with snap
  snap [options] <recording>                  A source time on screen: --at <s> moves to the nearest event, --event <kind> --index <n> names one; --lead <s> and --end work with both
  find-text [options] <recording> [texts...]  Every place a text (or --pattern, a regular expression) shows on a recording's screen, tracked through scrolls; hide them with the hideText op
  verify-hidden [options] <recording>         Export the edit (or read --movie), OCR its frames and list every output moment where a text, a pattern or the private data is still readable; exit 1 on a leak
  serve [options]                             Run the recorder service: the one owner of the recordings' edits while it runs, and the way to GenesisTools.app's recorder face (windows, renders, the camera), on <recordings>/service.sock with service.json beside it. A second start finds the first and exits; it exits after 10 minutes with no connection and no open edit, and when its code changes
  help [command]                              display help for command

Usage: recorder start [options]

Record a movie into the recordings library (screen.mp4 with audio tracks,
cursor.jsonl, recording.json), or with --frames the frames of the displays (JPEG
or the recorder's files, OCR into ocr.jsonl or beside each frame), as
recorder.start() in the REPL does. Runs until the stop command, the menu bar
item, the floating controls, Ctrl-C or --max-seconds; pausing leaves the paused
time out

Options:
  --audio <sources>           audio tracks: system, mic, or system,mic
  --mic-device <uid>          the microphone (an id from `ax-tool
                              audio-devices`; needs --audio mic)
  --fps <n>                   frames per second while something moves, 1–120 for
                              a movie (default 60), 0.5–120 with --frames
  --idle-fps <n>              frames per second while nothing moves, 0.1–5 (by
                              default the movie keeps --fps)
  --threshold <percent>       how much of the picture must change to leave the
                              idle rate, 0–100 (default 0.5)
  --display <index>           record only this display (NSScreen order); by
                              default the recording follows the pointer and the
                              focus to whichever screen is in use
  --window <ids>              record these windows (CG window ids, comma
                              separated)
  --app <name>                record this app's windows (name, bundle id or pid)
  --region <x,y,w,h>          record this area of a display, in screen points
                              from the top-left corner
  --exclude-window-ids <ids>  leave these windows out of the movie (CG window
                              ids, comma separated)
  --camera                    record the camera beside the screen into
                              camera.mov (the menu bar recorder records it and
                              must run; the editor draws the bubble)
  --countdown [seconds]       count down on screen before it records, 1–10 s
                              (bare: 3 s), as the capture picker does
  --title <text>              the recording's title in the library and the menu
  --max-seconds <n>           stop after this long, 1–14400 for a movie, 1–7200
                              with --frames (default 600)
  --no-indicator              no red border around what is recorded (never in
                              the movie either way)
  --no-shortcuts              do not keep the ⌘/⌃ shortcuts pressed (by default
                              they go into the cursor track for the keys
                              overlay; plain typing never does)
  --system-cursor             keep the system cursor for a display/area movie;
                              start a window/app movie with its editable cursor
                              hidden
  --no-controls               do not open the floating controls
  --open                      open the editor when the recording stops
  --json                      events and the result as JSON lines on stdout
  --frames [format]           record frames instead of a movie, as
                              recorder.start() in the REPL does: original (the
                              recorder's files, the default) or jpeg
  --jpeg-quality <q>          with --frames jpeg: the JPEG quality, 0.1–1
                              (default 0.75)
  --naming [naming]           with --frames: how frames are named, elapsed or
                              wall-clock or absolute
  --flush [when]              with --frames: finish (all at the stop) or piece
                              (each piece's frames land as the piece ends)
  --ocr                       with --frames: read the text of each kept frame
                              (Vision OCR)
  --ocr-languages <list>      with --frames: the OCR languages in order of
                              preference (en-US,cs-CZ); turns OCR on
  --ocr-min-chars <n>         with --frames: OCR text shorter than this is
                              stored as no text; turns OCR on
  --ocr-sink [sink]           with --frames: where the OCR goes, sidecar (a
                              <frame>.ocr.json beside each frame) or jsonl (one
                              ocr.jsonl row per frame)
  --displays <which>          with --frames: all, main (the default) or display
                              ids, comma separated
  --max-long-side <px>        with --frames: the longest side of a kept frame,
                              320–16384
  --heartbeat <seconds>       with --frames: a frame at least this often while
                              nothing changes, 0 is off
  --piece-seconds <n>         with --frames: the length of one capture piece,
                              5–180
  -h, --help                  display help for command

Usage: recorder trash [options] <recording...>

Move library recordings through the removal policy into the GenesisTools trash,
all in one call; the answer names the batch, when it drains and the tools rm
restore command that puts it back (tools rm trash lists it too; the window's
Move to Trash uses Finder's Trash). Run by an agent, or for a recording the
policy does not allow, it asks the user: every such recording goes into ONE
request they confirm with tools rm approve <id>. A meeting's screen recording is
refused, and then nothing is moved

Arguments:
  recording   library ids, `last` or recording folders

Options:
  --no-aside  keep the folders in the library while a request waits, instead of
              moving them aside
  --json      accepted for scripts; the output is the same with or without it
  -h, --help  display help for command

Usage: recorder comment [options] [command] <recording> <at> <text>

Add a review comment at a time of the edit (OUTPUT seconds or m:ss, what plays);
the editor shows it as a marker on the timeline. `comment add <recording> <at>
<text>` is the same command

Arguments:
  recording                             a library id, `last`, `open` or a
                                        recording folder
  at                                    where it is: seconds, m:ss or h:mm:ss of
                                        what plays
  text                                  the comment

Options:
  --to <time>                           the end of the commented range
  --author <name>                       who wrote it
  --link <url>                          the page it came from: a vitrinka
                                        annotation's link, a board's link (with
                                        --annotation), a PR
  --annotation <number>                 the annotation's number on the board
                                        --link names: the comment opens it
  --source                              at and --to are times of the recording
                                        itself, not of the edit
  --export                              at and --to are times of the exported
                                        file, as its player shows them (the
                                        intro card first); a time on a card goes
                                        onto the movie
  --json                                accepted for scripts; the output is the
                                        same with or without it
  -h, --help                            display help for command

Commands:
  import [options] <recording> <board>  Import a vitrinka board's annotations as
                                        review comments: each annotation on a
                                        shot, movie or step card (or on one
                                        --card) at the time its text starts with
                                        (0:42, 1:02:03, 42s), read on the
                                        exported file the board shows (the intro
                                        card's length comes off; a time on a
                                        card goes onto the movie with a note),
                                        else at 0:00 with a note; a second
                                        import adds nothing

Usage: recorder sheet [options] <recording>

Several frames on one PNG grid, each labelled with its time: the edit as it
exports (OUTPUT seconds) or, with --source, the recording as it was recorded
(SOURCE seconds, the seconds ops take)

Arguments:
  recording          a library id, `last`, a recording folder, a movie or an
                     edit.json

Options:
  --count <n>        frames spread over the range (default 6, at most 48)
  --every <seconds>  a frame every this many seconds over the range instead (a

  --from <time>      the range's start in seconds or m:ss (default 0)
  --to <time>        the range's end (default the end)

  --columns <n>      the grid's columns (default by the frames' shape, a near

  --out <png>        where the picture goes (default a temporary file)
  --json             accepted for scripts; the output is the same with or
                     without it
  -h, --help         display help for command
